lean.statement: For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space E, potential U:E→ℝ, and alpha,eta in NNReal with 0<alpha<=1, if U is C², alpha‖v‖² <= D²U(x)[v,v] <= ‖v‖² for every x,v, ‖gradient U(xref)‖² <= alpha·finrank ℝ E, and eta<=1, then, with μ=volume.tilted(-U) and piEta=gaussianSmoothing μ (sqrt eta), the squared phase quadratic Kantorovich infimum at parameter 1/alpha between (dirac xref)⊗stdGaussian and piEta⊗stdGaussian is at most ENNReal.ofReal(5·(1/alpha)·finrank ℝ E). No minimizer or critical point is supplied as an input.
approved_definition_context: NNReal is the type of nonnegative real numbers; alpha and eta are coerced to reals in the displayed expressions.

The tilted measure is the normalized exponential tilt of volume when its normalizing integral is finite. gaussianSmoothing adds independent centered Gaussian noise of the displayed standard deviation.
phaseWassersteinSq kappa is the infimum of the paper's squared M_kappa phase cost over couplings. The target and initial momentum laws are the same standard Gaussian.
ContDiff ℝ 2 U supplies genuine first and second Fréchet derivatives; the Hessian inequality is pointwise in x and v.
The conclusion is only a q=2 squared-cost bound. It contains no all-q concentration, Picard transition, final total-variation accuracy, or expected-query-cost claim.
